$comment: Aggregate initial/start-up delivery contract. The INDIVIDUAL main-bundle budget is not here: it stays in webpack.performance-budget.json, which webpack.prod.js enforces during the build itself. Enforced by scripts/verify-delivery-budget.mjs; see docs/tesserafin/web-delivery-budget.md. Raising a ceiling is a deliberate edit to this file, reviewed in a pull request with before/after numbers. Nothing rewrites it automatically - there is no --update-baseline.
htmlEntrypointsNote: The entrypoints html-webpack-plugin injects into index.html (webpack.common.js `chunks`). The theme entrypoints (themes/*) are deliberately absent: their stylesheets are fetched by the theme manager at runtime, one at a time, and are not part of what a cold visitor downloads first. The verifier cross-checks this list against the tags actually injected and fails if they diverge.
playbackCredentialsBootNote: #153-A1-R2 REMOVED ./lib/playbackCredentials/boot.ts from bootModules, because the module it anchored no longer exists. History, so the removal is not mistaken for a ceiling dodge: the first revision replaced @jellyfin/sdk's WebSocketService with a first-party TicketedWebSocketService, and Api.subscribe() is synchronous, so an eager shim had to occupy Api.webSocket before the first subscriber ran. That shim issued import('./install') at start-up, which pulled the broker, the duplicate socket runtime and the identity helpers into their own chunk - measured at 9760 B raw / 3106 B gzip / 2789 B brotli, one extra asset - and declaring boot.ts here is what made the budget COUNT those bytes instead of leaving them in no tier at all. That was the honest measurement, and it put four start-up metrics over ceiling with no ceiling raise authorized. The reshape removes the cause rather than the accounting: scripts/patch-jellyfin-sdk.mjs teaches the SHIPPED service to mint a fresh single-use ticket for every physical connection attempt, so there is no seam, no shim and no duplicate runtime. The ticket path lives inside node_modules.@jellyfin.sdk.bundle.js, an asset this budget already counts, so it adds no chunk and no asset. What is left of the credential machinery is the MEDIA broker, reached only from playback call sites through lib/playbackCredentials/broker.ts, which is not a boot module and whose import() is genuinely not issued until playback begins. bootModules describes reality: with nothing left to anchor, keeping boot.ts here would be as misleading as removing it to hide a chunk. The protectedModulePatterns rule `playback-credentials` below, plus ci/verify-credential-startup-boundary.mjs, are what prove no unconditional credential import escapes the start-up tier now that no boot module names one.
bootModulesNote: Modules whose `import()` calls run unconditionally at start-up. Their chunks are counted in the `startup` tier so that the budget cannot be dodged by moving a static start-up import behind `import()`: the bytes change tier, the total does not. Route-level `lazy()` boundaries are NOT listed - those are async on purpose and are governed by protectedModulePatterns instead.
countedAssetExtensionsNote: Anything else appearing in the counted set (a font, an image, a wasm module promoted into an initial chunk) is a hard failure, not a silent exclusion: it has to be classified deliberately here first.

startupGzipBump: 904192 -> 905216 in tesserafin-web #154 (S4, the console credential disclosure). THE BUNDLE GREW. The CI production build of the head commit measured startup.gzipBytes 904328 against the 904192 ceiling - 136 B over it - and that overshoot is what forced this bump. 905216 is this file's own rounding rule applied to that measurement: ceil(904328 / 1024) * 1024 = 884 KiB. A first revision of this note read the delivery-budget gate's HEADROOM column (`PASS (-1795)`, i.e. ceiling minus measurement) as if it were a base->head delta, and concluded that every other metric had fallen. It had not. Headroom against a ceiling inherited from the #129 baseline is not the effect of this change, and the two must never be confused. The real effect, from two cold `npm run build:production` runs on base e92babdc and head 541eedcc with identical node_modules (package-lock.json is byte-identical across the two commits) and both worktrees clean, is a small INCREASE in every byte metric: startup.rawBytes 3221343 -> 3221694 (+351), startup.gzipBytes 904141 -> 904300 (+159), startup.brotliBytes 571541 -> 571680 (+139); initial.rawJsBytes 1955479 -> 1955830 (+351), initial.rawBytes 2127291 -> 2127642 (+351), initial.gzipBytes 544009 -> 544168 (+159), initial.brotliBytes 458732 -> 458871 (+139); initial.rawCssBytes unchanged, and both asset counts unchanged at 25 and 45. A second head build reproduced startup.rawBytes 3221694 exactly. Per asset the whole effect is main.tesserafin.bundle.js raw 390502 -> 390853 (+351), gzip 106575 -> 106730 (+155), plus 4 gzip bytes in runtime.bundle.js. Raw, gzip and brotli all rose together and monotonically out of one asset, so this is NOT a compression-ratio artefact and NOT a net decrease. Minification strips comments, so the 351 B is emitted code: the endpoint-category logging implementation - src/utils/urlCategory.ts, and the `method`/`endpoint` locals it adds to src/utils/fetch.js. A small, reviewed payload addition, accepted deliberately as the cost of not printing a session credential to the console.

assetCountNote: initial.assetCount is a stable, small set - treat any movement as a real change. startup.assetCount is the metric most likely to need a mechanical bump: the tier counts whole chunk GROUPS, and splitChunks will happily extract a newly shared module out of one of them into two files. A count bump whose byte totals are unchanged is a chunk split, not growth; say so in the pull request and move on.
rounding: Every byte ceiling is the measurement rounded UP to the next whole KiB (1024 B). Asset counts take no margin: the measured count is the ceiling. The KiB margin exists only to absorb the handful of bytes that move when __COMMIT_SHA__ / __JF_BUILD_VERSION__ differ between a local build and a CI build (webpack.common.js, .github/workflows/__package.yml) - it is not headroom for features.

baseline.note: Measured on tesserafin-web main at the squash merge of PR #130, from two clean production builds with identical results. See docs/tesserafin/web-delivery-budget.md for the full asset table.

compression.gzip: node:zlib gzipSync, level 9, zlib defaults otherwise
compression.method: each asset compressed separately, sizes summed - assets are separate HTTP responses with separate compression contexts. Nothing compressed here is written to dist/.

protectedModulePatterns.reason: Theme Studio is an authoring tool reached from Display preferences, not a viewer destination (tesserafin-web #119). It must stay behind its async route: an ordinary viewer who never opens it must never download it.
Manifest and token validation is authoring/compiler-side work (#115, #117). The viewer resolves an already-valid presentation; it does not validate one at boot.

Content pack management and the generated ContentPacks client are a manager destination and a wizard step (tesserafin-web #139 M3), not something a cold visitor downloads. `content-packs-api.ts` alone is 61 KB of generated operations. The rule is load-bearing rather than decorative: a static import of `ContentPacksApi` into `apps/modern/routes/routes.tsx` - a module that IS in main.tesserafin.bundle.js - fails this boundary, and that is the `eager-feature-import` control in the deliberate-break matrix. Note that `apps/modern/components/AppToolbar` is NOT eager: it is behind `lazy: () => import('../AppLayout')`, so an import there is legitimately async and this rule correctly stays silent about it.

Item Details is the largest single viewer route (tesserafin-web #129 Step 1b). It replaced a view-manager controller that was already async, and it must stay async: a cold visitor who never opens an item must never download it. Navigating to /details is what first requests this chunk.

#153-A1-R2. The media capability broker is wanted only once playback begins, and it is the single largest thing the credential work adds (~9.8 KB raw across broker, install and identity). It must stay behind the import() issued by lib/playbackCredentials/broker.ts and must never be reachable from the initial or start-up graph: a static import of any of these three into an eagerly reached module is what the first revision did by accident, and it cost four start-up metrics. Note this rule is only HALF the guarantee - webpack's module concatenation can hide a member's identifier from the chunk module list, so ci/verify-credential-startup-boundary.mjs asserts the same boundary at source level, where concatenation cannot reach.

acceptanceRuleForItemDetails: tesserafin-web #129 Step 1b, SATISFIED: the modern Item Details route is registered through ASYNC_USER_ROUTES / toAsyncPageRoute in both route families, and the `item-details` protectedModulePatterns entry above enforces its absence from the initial and start-up graphs. No ceiling was raised for it.
